the Cox model with a time-dependent covariate is a special case of the multi-state model with a time-invariant covariate.
the multi-state regression model with the intermediate event approach is more efficient than the Cox model with the time-dependent covariaties approach.
the Cox model with a time-dependent covariate can be used as a substitute for the multi-state model with a discrete covariate if the covariate changes only once during the study.

the multi-state regression models provide a more accurate representation of survival time than the Cox regression model with time-dependent (discretized) covariates.
the Cox model with the time-dependent covariatives is more flexible than the other multi-state models and it should be used as the default approach.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cox model with a time-dependent covariate and the multi-state regression model with an intermediate event yield similar parameter estimates.
the multi-state models are more flexible in modeling time-dependent covariaties and the results from these models can be easily interpreted in the context of the disease progression.
the Cox model with a time-dependent covariate is a good approximation to a multi-state model when there are no unobserved intermediate events.

, in many situations, the multi-state model is a better model to analyze survival data when there are time-dependent covariaties.
